radiusSource: Radius 7.119e8 cm and mass 8.211e27 g from Agol et al. (2021, PSJ 2, 1; doi:10.3847/PSJ/abd022), Table 6, which combines their transit-timing masses with the photodynamic radius ratios and the Mann et al. (2019) stellar mass. GM from that mass and the CODATA gravitational constant 6.67430e-20 km^3 kg^-1 s^-2. A sphere: no oblateness of these planets is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Agol et al. (2021, PSJ 2, 1; doi:10.3847/PSJ/abd022), Table 2 (transit-timing analysis): 1.510826 d

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, visible colour or oblateness of TRAPPIST-1b is measured. Its 15 µm temperature lens is a bare-rock model this project fitted to JWST light curves (see the README).

massSource: 1.374 +/- 0.069 Earth masses from E. Agol et al. (2021), Refining the Transit-timing and Photometric Analysis of TRAPPIST-1, PSJ 2, 1, Table 6: the transit-timing mass ratio times the Mann et al. (2019) stellar mass.
insolationSource: 4.153 times Earth's insolation, E. Agol et al. (2021), Refining the Transit-timing and Photometric Analysis of TRAPPIST-1, PSJ 2, 1, Table 6.
semiMajorAxisSource: 0.01154 au, E. Agol et al. (2021), Refining the Transit-timing and Photometric Analysis of TRAPPIST-1, PSJ 2, 1, Table 6.
